limitations: Native request is not proof that a destination constructor executed.
Class name is read through top-level base vtable getter, not inferred from ID or registration order.
Source candidates are proximity-attributed and are not yet verified full call graph owners.
0x30/48 is not registered and is kept as a dispatcher sentinel.
phase_slots records the 10 contiguous callback pointers (offset +0x08..+0x2C); the earlier +0x30/+0x34 words are adjacent data, not phase callbacks.
ID 1 looks up, directly invokes, and calls virtual methods on ID 2. These are proven cross-app calls, not child-creation APIs or proof of a parent-child stack relationship.
ID 6→3 is now ELF-supported as a conditional transition request via dynamic byte +0x2A, not a generic parent return. Runtime branch outcome and factory execution remain unobserved.

The generic 0x3DFC1C request has a caller-supplied destination, not a missing application class. ID20/ID25 exit requests and internal recursive cancellation use sentinel 0x30. Other dynamic factory lookups and runtime dispatch outcomes remain unresolved.

The root scheduler can invoke actual constructors through 0x3F1BA0 -> BSS factory jalr at 0x3F1BE0 and store active root pointer 0x63BE38. Recovered control flow is not proof any particular factory executed during the user's run.

The historical label 'factory lookup' at 0x3F1C40 is shorthand for a provider that actually invokes BSS factory jalr at 0x3F1C78; it does not install the global root pointer. Whether factories return cached objects or allocate anew is class-specific and remains to be verified.

child_successor.semantics: Only an observable child at phase 6 can supply its pending successor to parent.child_id. Native code looks up the successor and may initialize and update it; no claim that either factory succeeded without runtime evidence.

demo_main_exit.semantics: ID 6 default exit target is ID 3 after initialization. Choice1 signals exit with target unchanged, whereas choice3 overwrites target ID 6. The exit condition and child-activity probe gate the dynamic request; no factory execution is established.

fight_result_dispatch.semantics: The ID28 phase3 callback directly calls 0x40BC90. Selector 1 selects result child ID29 or 30 via predicate; selector2 child ID34; selector3 child ID38. Default target 0x30 is sentinel, not a registered child. The helper requests via 0x3DFBD0 without proving creation.

cancel_and_forward_dispatch.source: exact SDBZ EU-beta ELF, no runtime path claims

forwarded_child_request.action: Forward caller-supplied child ID to existing child through 0x3DFB00; clear parent suppression flag 0x04. If current child lookup yields no instance, the helper instead stores requested ID in +0x12 and attempts lookup/parent metadata propagation; it does not use this forwarded callsite.

recursive_cancel.action: Entering pending transition from phases 1..4 requests 0x30 on existing child when lookup resolves. It may be rejected by child's own flag 0x01.

fight_demo_end_timeout.condition: unordered-or-greater comparison versus threshold (MIPS c.ole.s then bc1f). Timer may have been accumulated based on global flag -0xE62(gp), but no runtime delta is assumed.

fight_play_single_finish.condition: phase-4 callback reaches jump-table case 9 and completion predicate returns zero; then two cleanup calls precede request 0x30

native_root_factory_dispatch.phase5_transition_guard: phase=5, child ID sentinel or suppression bit4 set; virtual +0x44 returns nonzero; status-word bit31 clear; parent ID=0x30; then calls 0x3F1BA0 with byte+0x10
native_root_factory_dispatch.semantics: Scheduler phase5 root (parent ID sentinel 0x30) invokes 0x3F1BA0 on pending ID. 0x3F1BA0 initializes registration, range-checks ID 1..47 after byte mask, loads BSS factory pointer, jalr invokes factory and stores returned root pointer (or fallback) at 0x63BE38. Invalid IDs select a static fallback pointer. This is an actual factory invocation instruction path but its execution in a recorded game run is unobserved. Distinguish the other function 0x3F1C40: it ALSO calls a factory via jalr at 0x3F1C78, returning the provider's object pointer without writing the active root global. Neither code path proves execution during a user-captured run.
